correctness.rationale: Fix positive integer n=ord_e(q), with coprime q,e>=2, and let m(q,e) be the least number of q-power summands with repetitions allowed producing zero modulo e. If m(q,e)=3 and 3 does not divide n, normalize exponents to 0<=a<=b<n and form F(X)=1+X^a+X^b. F and X^n-1 have no common complex root: three unit complex numbers summing to zero must be a regular 3-gon, whose ratios force a cubic root of unity and hence 3|n. Thus their nonzero integral resultant is divisible by e; each factor F(zeta) for zeta^n=1 has modulus<=3, so e<=3^n. If 3|n, F_n(X)=1+X^{n/3}+X^{2n/3} vanishes at primitive n-th roots, so Phi_n(X) divides F_n(X). For all sufficiently large integer bases q, nonzero resultants of Phi_n(X) with X^d-1 (d proper divisor of n) ensure ord_{Phi_n(q)}(q)=n. If n odd choose e=Phi_n(q), and no 2-sum is possible in an odd-order group. If n even, hence 6|n, choose q>=2 congruent 1 mod3 and e=3Phi_n(q); since Phi_n(1)=1 for such n, gcd(q,e)=1, order remains n, 1+q^{n/3}+q^{2n/3} vanishes mod e, and no 2-sum exists because every q-power is 1 mod3. Infinitely many growing moduli result. Independent exact resultant tests for 3-free orders and construction samples n=3,6,9,12,15 matched. The n=1 and n=2 finite-side boundaries are included in the general argument.
residual_risks: The bound e<=3^n is universal but not claimed optimal; the theorem does not enumerate the finite exceptional moduli.
The cyclic-order argument requires gcd(q,e)=1 and m defined with positive number of summands and repetitions allowed.
The large-q exact-order lemma invokes finitely many nonzero resultants; finite sample checks are not proof of unbounded n.

originality.rationale: The published 2021 Breuer–Héthelyi–Horváth–Külshammer Lemma 2.11 gives m(q,p^k)=3 when the odd multiplicative order has a factor three, so the odd-order infinite construction is substantially covered in spirit and follows from that lemma together with primes congruent 1 mod n. This is credited; it is NOT the claimed new core. That same lemma gives m=2 for even order on odd prime-power moduli, so it cannot imply the new even-order three-sum construction with composite modulus 3Phi_n(q). Jacob–Külshammer Proposition 11 establishes finiteness only with the extra hypothesis e|Phi_n(q) and a smaller length threshold, whereas this theorem fixes ord_e(q)=n over arbitrary composite moduli and supplies the explicit bound 3^n for every n not divisible by three. Lam–Leung classifies weight sets of complex root-of-unity sums in characteristic zero, not these modular residue zero sums or their bounded moduli. Comparisons were by hypotheses and implications, including the genuine earlier odd-order coverage. No all-order exact finite/infinite statement for arbitrary modulus was identified in full relevant primary sources or mathematical-record search.
residual_risks: A broader classical group-ring/resolvent theorem might implicitly yield the modulus bound or composite construction; searches did not find a covering all-order statement.
Odd-order infinite side largely follows earlier results and is not independently credited as new; independent contribution must be evaluated via complete dichotomy and even-order side.

value.rationale: The invariant m(q,e) is central in a published modular power-sum problem, and multiplicative order is its natural arithmetic organizing parameter. The theorem identifies an exact all-order finite/infinite boundary at divisibility by three, provides an explicit bound for every order outside the infinite regime, and constructs infinitely many genuinely composite moduli for the even-order regime where prime-power results cannot have minimal length three. These are structural classifications, not a single example; their value persists even though earlier papers cover the odd-order existence subcase.
residual_risks: Universal bound is not asserted sharp; classification gives a dichotomy rather than a complete list below 3^n.

limitations: Odd-order infinite construction is substantially anticipated by prime-power results; only the full all-n classification and composite-even extension survive as claimed additions.
